records.transcript: Let's discuss the role of startup incubators in supporting new businesses. These are programs designed to help startups navigate the early stages of development and increase their chances of success by providing resources, mentorship, and networking. What resources might a new business lack? Incubators often provide office space and equipment to help start ups get off the ground, and they also steer new businesses toward funding opportunities. Many new entrepreneurs will lack the financial means to invest in basic necessities themselves, and this support can be invaluable. Another important element of incubators is mentorship. Experienced professionals and industry experts offer guidance and advice to start up founders. Starting a business is full of pitfalls, and a good mentor can help you avoid some of the more common ones, not to mention refine your business strategies. Networking opportunities are another significant benefit of incubators. What does a new enterprise need more than anything else? Investors. Being part of an incubator program allows you to connect with potential investors, other entrepreneurs, and future business partners. Now, participating in an incubator is not without its challenges. There's a lot of competition to get into some of these programs, so not all startups are accepted. Once you've been accepted, the pressure to perform and meet milestones can be intense, and failure to do so can lose you the support of the incubator. That said, the benefits can be substantial. Incubators provide a supportive environment that fosters innovation and helps startups overcome the hurdles of early stage development.

records.transcript: A remarkable discovery was made in the 1970s. I'm referring to the Bactrian Gold, which dates to around the first century BCE and includes over twenty thousand objects. It's called Bactrian Gold, but the treasure includes jewelry, coins, and ornaments. It came from six burial mounds belonging to five women and one man. They would have been wealthy nomads from Central Asia or northwestern China. The discovery was so important to archaeologists that it was compared to the discovery of King Tut's tomb in Egypt. Bactrian Gold was found at a major crossroads of the Silk Road, the ancient trade routes that connected Europe and Asia. The Silk Road was not a single road but a vast network of trade routes. It facilitated the exchange not only of goods, but also of ideas, art, and technology. The Bactrian Gold artifacts show Greek, Indian, and Chinese influences, and some pieces combine elements from several cultures. These many influences passed through the region because it was a crossroads. The discovery provides significant insight into how interconnected the ancient world truly was. It serves as a testament to the Silk Road's role in fostering culture and commerce long before the modern era.

records.transcript: Let's step into the curious world of trompe l'oeil, a painting technique that doesn't just play with perspective. It plays with your perception. The term, French for deceive the eye, hints at its magic. Paintings so convincing, they make you question what's real. Trompe l'oeil paintings often look three dimensional and blur the boundaries between what's real and what isn't. Though its roots stretch back to ancient Greece and Rome, trompe l'oeil truly flourished during the Renaissance. Artists like Andrea Mantegna used the technique to make ceilings look like open skies, creating the impression that rooms were open to the heavens. By the 17th century, trompe l'oeil had become a popular form of interior decoration. Consider the work of Dutch artist Samuel van Hoogstraten, whose paintings gave viewers the illusion of stepping into another room or looking through a window. These paintings play tricks on the viewer's sense of space and depth, creating a sense of wonder. Not everyone is enchanted. Some view trompe l'oeil as a clever trick, technically impressive, but emotionally hollow. It's a fair critique. When art leans heavily on illusion, it risks being seen as spectacle rather than substance. Still, the technique endures, and today's artists push it further, using digital tools to bend reality in ways that go beyond paint and canvas. Trompe l'oeil isn't just about fooling the eye anymore. It's about challenging how we see.

transcriptSentences.text: Let's step into the curious world of trompe l'oeil, a painting technique that doesn't just play with perspective.
It plays with your perception.
The term, French for deceive the eye, hints at its magic.
Paintings so convincing, they make you question what's real.
Trompe l'oeil paintings often look three dimensional and blur the boundaries between what's real and what isn't.
Though its roots stretch back to ancient Greece and Rome, trompe l'oeil truly flourished during the Renaissance.
Artists like Andrea Mantegna used the technique to make ceilings look like open skies, creating the impression that rooms were open to the heavens.
By the 17th century, trompe l'oeil had become a popular form of interior decoration.
Consider the work of Dutch artist Samuel van Hoogstraten, whose paintings gave viewers the illusion of stepping into another room or looking through a window.
These paintings play tricks on the viewer's sense of space and depth, creating a sense of wonder.
Not everyone is enchanted.
Some view trompe l'oeil as a clever trick, technically impressive, but emotionally hollow.
It's a fair critique.
When art leans heavily on illusion, it risks being seen as spectacle rather than substance.
Still, the technique endures, and today's artists push it further, using digital tools to bend reality in ways that go beyond paint and canvas.
Trompe l'oeil isn't just about fooling the eye anymore.
It's about challenging how we see.

records.transcript: Imagine stepping into a gallery where the walls don't just display art, they move with you. One moment, a sculpture spins gently in the breeze. The next, a panel shifts as you walk by. Welcome to the world of kinetic art, a mesmerizing fusion of motion and visual storytelling. Born in the early 20th century, kinetic art is still pushing boundaries, constantly redefining what art can be. Unlike static paintings or marble sculptures, kinetic pieces come alive. Think of Alexander Calder's mobiles, delicately balanced to sway with the air, or Theo Janssen's strand beasts, giant wind powered creatures that walk across beaches like living machines. These works don't just sit there, they respond, they evolve. Hungarian artist Laszlo Moholy Nagy, one of the movement's pioneers, believed light and motion could transform how we experience art. Moholy Nagy created a groundbreaking piece called Light Space Modulator, a motorized sculpture of spinning metal and glass, more of a performance than an object. But kinetic art isn't always smooth sailing. Incorporating motors and sensors means dealing with breakdowns, software glitches, and constant upkeep. Some critics argue that the tech can overshadow the artistry, turning installations into flashy gimmicks. Still, the genre thrives. From interactive digital landscapes to whimsical mechanical sculptures, kinetic art invites us into a multi sensory experience, one that's immersive, unpredictable, and unforgettable.

records.transcript: You know, modern LED light bulbs have really changed the way we light our homes and workplaces. They're extremely energy efficient. But before LEDs took over, incandescent bulbs were the norm for everyday lighting needs. Incandescent bulbs give off a warm, full spectrum glow, including the wavelength called near infrared light, which is invisible to the human eye. Now, LEDs are designed to shine in the visible range, about 400 to 700 nanometers, a relatively narrow band of the spectrum, which is great for saving energy and thus for reducing costs. But by cutting out near infrared from the artificial light we're exposed to, we might be missing out on some subtle, but important health benefits. Research suggests that exposure to near infrared light may support cardiovascular health, reduce stress, and even boost your mood, kind of like the light from a campfire or a bright sunny day. Incandescent bulbs, though less efficient, might offer physiological benefits that LEDs lack. Despite these limitations, LED bulbs remain a positive, popular and practical choice. But the question is, are the downsides worth it? Many experts say no, and they're advocating instead for advanced LED systems that bring near infrared back into the mix. Such systems do exist, but they're pricey, sometimes ten times more than regular LEDs. So, for now at least, they're mostly used in specialized medical settings.

records.transcript: Today I'd like to talk about the color blue in art. Now, we might take blue for granted, but for centuries it was one of the most elusive and expensive pigments an artist could use. In ancient Egypt, artisans crafted blue from lapis lazuli, a brilliant stone mined in what is now Afghanistan. This mineral was so rare and so valuable that it was literally worth its weight in gold. Because of its scarcity, blue was reserved for the most honored subjects in art. In medieval European paintings, important holy figures were often cloaked in deep blue robes. This wasn't just symbolic; it was also a financial statement. During the Renaissance, oil paints made the mixing and layering of colors, including the mixing of lapis lazuli powder with oil. Still, blue remained costly due to its natural sources. Then came a turning point in the 18th century. Synthetic dyes. Prussian blue, which was originally created in Germany quite by accident, was affordable, vibrant, and widely accessible. Suddenly, artists from all walks of life could use blue freely. The democratization of color transformed artistic expression and opened doors for artistic movements like impressionism, where blue was used freely to evoke mood, atmosphere, and emotion. Even today, blue carries echoes of its luxurious past. It's often linked to ideas of calm, depth, and aspiration. Yet some traditionalists still argue that no synthetic pigment can match the richness and depth of lapis lazuli. The story of blue continues to reflect the evolving relationship between art, innovation, and culture.
records.translation:
今天我想谈谈艺术中的蓝色。
我们现在可能觉得蓝色是理所当然的，但几个世纪以来，它一直是艺术家能使用的最难以捉摸、最昂贵的颜料之一。
在古埃及，工匠们用青金石制作蓝色，这是一种在现在的阿富汗开采的华丽石头。
这种矿物质如此稀有和珍贵，以至于它的价值简直是等同于同等重量的黄金。
由于它的稀缺性，蓝色被保留用于艺术中最受尊崇的主题。
在中世纪的欧洲绘画中，重要的圣人形象经常披着深蓝色的长袍。
这不仅仅是象征性的；它也是一份财务声明。
文艺复兴时期，油画使得颜色的混合和分层成为可能，包括将青金石粉末与油混合。
尽管如此，由于其天然来源，蓝色仍然昂贵。
然后，18世纪出现了一个转折点。
那就是合成染料。
普鲁士蓝最初在德国偶然被创造出来，它价格实惠、色彩鲜艳且易于获取。
突然间，各行各业的艺术家都可以自由使用蓝色了。
色彩的民主化改变了艺术表达，并为印象派等艺术运动打开了大门，在这些运动中，蓝色被自由地用来唤起情绪、氛围和情感。
即使在今天，蓝色也带有其奢华过去的 echoes（回响）。
它通常与平静、深度和抱负的理念联系在一起。
然而，一些传统主义者仍然认为，没有任何合成颜料能与青金石的丰富性和深度相媲美。
蓝色的故事继续反映着艺术、创新和文化之间不断演变的关系。

records.transcript: Soft power refers to a country's ability to influence others through attraction, culture, and collaboration. The term was introduced by political scientist Joseph Nye in 1990. He noticed that some countries gain support not by using force or money, but by being admired and respected. What Nye contributed wasn't just a name. He offered a clear framework for understanding this kind of influence. He explained that power works in three ways: by forcing others, by paying them, or by attracting them. That third kind, attraction, is what he called soft power. By classifying power this way, he made it easier for people to understand and talk about influence that comes from trust, culture, and values. A modern example is South Korea's cultural wave, which has sparked global interest in Korean pop music, language, and food. This kind of appeal fits directly into Nye's idea of attraction. It shows how cultural influence can build admiration and shape international relationships without pressure or incentives. Now, soft power takes time because it's built on trust, reputation, and emotional connection. It spreads through cultural events, learning opportunities, and other shared experiences, things that grow gradually. But once established, it tends to last, often shaping how future generations view a country. Like planting a tree, it needs patience and care, but its roots run deep and its impact endures.
records.translation:
软实力是指一个国家通过吸引力、文化和合作来影响他国的能力。
这个术语由政治学家约瑟夫·奈在1990年提出。
他注意到，有些国家获得支持不是通过使用武力或金钱，而是通过受人钦佩和尊重。
奈的贡献不仅仅是一个名字。
他提供了一个清晰的框架来理解这种影响力。
他解释说，权力有三种运作方式：强迫他人、支付他人或吸引他人。
第三种方式，即吸引力，就是他所说的软实力。
通过这种方式对权力进行分类，他使人们更容易理解和谈论来自信任、文化和价值观的影响力。
一个现代的例子是韩国的文化浪潮，它在全球范围内激发了人们对韩国流行音乐、语言和食物的兴趣。
这种吸引力直接符合奈的吸引力理论。
它展示了文化影响力如何在没有压力或激励的情况下建立钦佩并塑造国际关系。
现在，软实力需要时间，因为它建立在信任、声誉和情感联系之上。
它通过文化活动、学习机会和其他共享经验传播，这些事物是逐渐增长的。
但一旦建立起来，它往往会持久，经常塑造未来几代人对一个国家的看法。
就像种一棵树，它需要耐心和照料，但它的根扎得很深，其影响是持久的。

records.transcript: Positive reinforcement is a powerful concept in psychology and behavior training. It means giving a reward after someone performs an action you want them to do again. The basic idea is that when a behavior leads to a positive outcome, it's more likely to be repeated. In other words, we tend to repeat actions that bring us something positive. This principle applies to both humans and animals, but the way it works can differ. Animals need to receive rewards immediately after the desired behavior. For example, if a dog sits and gets a treat right away, it learns that sitting leads to something good. If the reward comes too late, the connection is lost. Humans, however, can understand delayed rewards. They might work hard today because they're aiming for a future goal, like earning a degree. Or they might feel motivated by praise even if the reward isn't tangible or instant. But rewards must be used carefully. If a parent gives a child candy to stop whining, the child may learn that whining gets rewarded. It's like watering weeds instead of flowers. You're encouraging the wrong behavior. And if rewards are given too frequently, they can reduce a person's internal motivation, making them rely more on external incentives to take action. So while positive reinforcement is effective, it works best when applied thoughtfully and with clear intent.
records.translation:
正向强化是心理学和行为训练中一个强大的概念。
它指的是在某人完成你希望他们再次做的行动后给予奖励。
基本思想是，当一个行为导致积极结果时，它更有可能被重复。
换句话说，我们倾向于重复那些给我们带来积极事物的行动。
这个原则适用于人类和动物，但它的作用方式可能有所不同。
动物需要在期望行为发生后立即获得奖励。
例如，如果一只狗坐下后立即得到奖励，它就会知道坐下会带来好东西。
如果奖励来得太晚，这种联系就会消失。
然而，人类可以理解延迟的奖励。
他们可能今天努力工作，因为他们瞄准一个未来的目标，比如获得一个学位。
或者他们可能会因为表扬而受到激励，即使奖励不是有形的或即时的。
但奖励必须小心使用。
如果父母给孩子糖果来停止哭闹，孩子可能会学会哭闹会得到奖励。
这就像给杂草浇水而不是给鲜花浇水。
你正在鼓励错误的行为。
而且，如果奖励过于频繁，它们会降低一个人的内在动机，使他们更依赖外部激励来采取行动。
因此，虽然正向强化是有效的，但当它经过深思熟虑并带有明确意图地应用时，效果最佳。

The basic idea is that when a behavior leads to a positive outcome, it's more likely to be repeated.
In other words, we tend to repeat actions that bring us something positive.
This principle applies to both humans and animals, but the way it works can differ.
Animals need to receive rewards immediately after the desired behavior.
For example, if a dog sits and gets a treat right away, it learns that sitting leads to something good.
If the reward comes too late, the connection is lost.
Humans, however, can understand delayed rewards.
They might work hard today because they're aiming for a future goal, like earning a degree.
Or they might feel motivated by praise even if the reward isn't tangible or instant.
But rewards must be used carefully.
If a parent gives a child candy to stop whining, the child may learn that whining gets rewarded.
It's like watering weeds instead of flowers.
You're encouraging the wrong behavior.
And if rewards are given too frequently, they can reduce a person's internal motivation, making them rely more on external incentives to take action.
So while positive reinforcement is effective, it works best when applied thoughtfully and with clear intent.

records.transcript: Expressionism is an influential modernist art movement that emerged in the early 20th century. This movement is characterized by its focus on representing emotional experience rather than physical reality. Expressionist artists aim to convey their inner feelings and perceptions through distorted and exaggerated forms, vivid colors, and bold brushstrokes. One of the most famous Expressionist artists is Edvard Munch. His painting The Scream shows an agonized person crying out. It eventually became an icon of the movement's focus on intense personal experience. Expressionism was not limited to visual arts, however. It also influenced literary theater and cinematic arts. In literature, authors like Franz Kafka explored themes of alienation and existential angst in his bizarre, dreamlike fiction. Expressionist theater often used dramatic lighting and intense performances to evoke emotional responses. Set sometimes featured oversized symbolic objects. In Elmer Rice's 1923 play The Adding Machine, a giant adding machine represents the dehumanizing forces of technology. Similarly, the German Expressionist film movement used innovative techniques, such as cutting between scenes with a shared sound to help create emotionally charged narratives. Despite its impact, Expressionism faced criticism for its departure from traditional aesthetics and its emphasis on the personal. Critics argued that its focus on subjective emotion robbed the works of broader content or meaning. And the bold brushwork in painting was sometimes viewed as lacking in skill and technique. Nonetheless, Expressionism paved the way for later movements such as Surrealism, leaving a lasting legacy in the art world.
records.translation:
表现主义是20世纪初出现的一个有影响力的现代主义艺术运动。
这场运动的特点是，它侧重于表现情感体验而非物理现实。
表现主义艺术家旨在通过扭曲和夸张的形式、鲜艳的色彩和大胆的笔触来传达他们的内心感受和认知。
最著名的表现主义艺术家之一是爱德华·蒙克。

它最终成为了这场运动专注于强烈个人体验的标志。
然而，表现主义不仅限于视觉艺术。
它还影响了文学戏剧和电影艺术。
在文学领域，像弗朗茨·卡夫卡这样的作家在他的怪诞、梦幻般的小说中探索了异化和存在主义焦虑的主题。
表现主义戏剧常使用戏剧性的灯光和强烈的表演来唤起情感反应。
布景有时会以超大的象征性物品为特色。
在埃尔默·赖斯1923年的戏剧《算术机》中，一台巨大的算术机代表了技术的非人化力量。

尽管如此，表现主义为后来的超现实主义等运动铺平了道路，在艺术界留下了持久的遗产。

records.transcript: A common theme in literature is isolation, and that's what we'll explore today. Isolation can be a powerful motif, reflecting the psychological effects of being separated from society. One of the most classic examples of isolation in literature is Mary Shelley's Frankenstein. In this novel, Victor Frankenstein's grotesque creation, the creature experiences profound isolation due to his monstrous appearance and the fear he instills in people. This isolation leads to anger and a desire for revenge, thus highlighting the detrimental effects of being ostracized. Another notable example is The Catcher in the Rye by J D Salinger. The protagonist, Holden Caulfield, feels disconnected from the world around him, and he struggles with alienation and loneliness. This social isolation is what drives Holden's actions and internal conflicts throughout the book. Yet another example of isolation in literature, and one that ends badly, is Herman Melville's Moby Dick. In this novel, Captain Ahab's obsessive, vengeful quest for the white whale leads to his isolation. This obsession distances him from his crew as well as his humanity, and it propels him and his ship toward a destructive end. However, the portrayal of isolation in literature is not always negative. In Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre, the titular character experiences isolation at various points in her life, such as when she is sent to live with her unkind relatives and later when she experiences loneliness at a boarding school. But Jane is resilient in the face of isolation, becoming strong and independent.

You can probably imagine people sitting in a Greek amphitheater, completely absorbed by the sounds filling the air. But music wasn't only heard in theater performances. It played a role in all kinds of settings, including religious ceremonies and athletic competitions. One instrument that stands out is the aulos. This aulos is a double reeded wind instrument that was a big part of Greek musical life, and it has a distinctive design. It has two pipes, each with a reed, usually made from a plant, similar to what you'd find in a modern oboe. And because the pipes are cylindrical, not conical like some other wind instruments, it produces a sound that's rich and sharp. That unique sound helped bring out emotion in plays and public events, which brought depth to the drama unfolding on stage. To really master the aulos, the player had to be highly skilled. One technique they used was circular breathing. It means inhaling air through the nose while simultaneously pushing air out through the cheeks. This allowed them to play long, continuous passages without stopping for breath. Even though the aulos was hugely important in ancient times, it eventually faded from use as other instruments and musical styles took over. Still, its legacy lives on as it gives us a glimpse into the musical world of ancient Greece.

records.transcript: Have you ever been so engrossed in a task that you completely missed something obvious? This is called inattentional blindness, a phenomenon where concentrating on one thing can make us overlook something happening right in front of us. A classic study illustrates this perfectly. Participants watched a video of people passing a basketball and were asked to count passes made by players in white shirts. Midway through the video, a person in a gorilla suit walked into the scene, thumped its chest and left. Astonishingly, about half the viewers never saw the gorilla. Their attention was locked on counting passes. In real world situations, inattentional blindness can have serious consequences. For example, while driving, focusing on finding a street sign might make you miss a pedestrian stepping into the road. Recognizing this tendency can help us stay safer and more aware. Interestingly, psychologists trace this phenomenon to a useful ability, selective attention. This is the brain's way of filtering sensory input to avoid overload, allowing us to concentrate on important tasks. Think about sitting in a noisy open plan office writing a report. Phones are ringing, people are talking, but you manage to tune it all out and focus on your work. That's selective attention at its best.
records.translation:
你有没有过这样一种经历：全神贯注于某项任务，以至于完全忽略了显而易见的事情？
这就是所谓的“非注意性盲视”，一种当我们专注于某件事时，会让我们忽略眼前发生的事情的现象。
一项经典研究完美地说明了这一点。
参与者观看了一段人们传篮球的视频，并被要求计算穿白衬衫的球员传球的次数。
视频播放到一半时，一个穿着大猩猩服装的人走进画面，捶打自己的胸部，然后离开了。
令人惊讶的是，大约一半的观众从未看到那只大猩猩。
他们的注意力完全集中在数传球次数上。
在现实生活中，非注意性盲视可能会产生严重的后果。
例如，在开车时，专注于寻找路标可能会让你错过一个走上马路的行人。
认识到这种倾向可以帮助我们保持更安全、更警觉。
有趣的是，心理学家将这种现象追溯到一种有用的能力——选择性注意力。
这是大脑过滤感官输入以避免超载的方式，使我们能够专注于重要的任务。
想象一下，你坐在一个嘈杂的开放式办公室里写报告。
电话铃响，人们在交谈，但你却能将这些都屏蔽掉，专注于你的工作。
这就是选择性注意力发挥到极致的表现。

records.transcript: There are many different factors that influence human behavior. One is related to social influence, or the idea that our behavior can be shaped by group pressure. To test this idea, a psychologist named Solomon Asch conducted a famous study in the 1950s, which has become hugely influential in the field. In his experiment, Asch invited American university students to take part in a simple visual judgment task. Each participant was placed in a group of seven to nine people, all but one of whom were working with the researcher. The group members were shown a standard line on one card and three comparison lines on another card. One comparison line matched the standard, while the other two were clearly different lengths. Basically, the correct choice was totally obvious. Each person announced aloud which line matched the standard, and those who were in on the study deliberately gave the wrong answer first. The real participant answered last. Across 12 trials, 75% of participants conformed with the incorrect answers that people in the group had given before them at least once, so they chose the line that was clearly wrong. This indicates strong influence of group pressure. This study was replicated in 1980, roughly 30 years after Asch conducted his experiment. The subjects in this experiment were British university students. Interestingly, conformity was much lower with these participants. This suggests that conformity may be influenced by culture and the country people grow up in.
records.translation:
有许多不同的因素会影响人类行为。
其中之一与社会影响有关，或者说，我们的行为可以受到群体压力的影响。
为了验证这个想法，一位名叫所罗门·阿施的心理学家在20世纪50年代进行了一项著名的研究，这项研究在该领域产生了巨大影响。
在他的实验中，阿施邀请美国大学生参加一个简单的视觉判断任务。
每位参与者被分到一个由七到九人组成的组中，其中除了一个人之外，其他人都与研究员合作。
小组成员会看到一张卡片上的标准线和另一张卡片上的三条比较线。
其中一条比较线与标准线匹配，而另外两条则明显长度不同。
基本上，正确的选择是完全显而易见的。
每个人都大声宣布哪条线与标准线匹配，而那些参与研究的人则故意先给出错误的答案。
真正的参与者最后回答。
在12次试验中，75%的参与者至少有一次顺从了小组中其他人之前给出的错误答案，所以他们选择了明显错误的线。
这表明群体压力具有强大的影响力。
这项研究在1980年被复制，大约是阿施进行实验30年后。
这次实验的受试者是英国大学生。
有趣的是，这些参与者的从众性要低得多。
这表明从众性可能受到文化和人们成长国家的影响。

records.transcript: Some years ago, the government of Tanzania in Africa proposed building a 452 kilometer paved road in the north of the country, with the goal of boosting transportation and economic growth. The proposed route, though, would go through Serengeti National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and conservationists raised alarms. The road would bisect the annual migration corridor of wildebeests and other animals, potentially putting enormous pressure on their populations and disrupting the ecosystem in general. The models used by the conservationists showed that blocking the corridor with the road could reduce wildebeest populations by up to one third, disrupt predator prey dynamics and fragment an ecosystem that supports lions, cheetahs and countless other species. Increased traffic would also heighten poaching risks and introduce invasive species. The evidence wasn't conclusive, but because the risk was so serious and the consequences probably irreversible, the government decided to halt the project. That decision reflects what's known as the precautionary principle. When an action or policy poses a plausible risk of serious or irreversible harm, we shouldn't wait for absolute scientific certainty before deciding what to do. Why is this important? The consequences of indecision can be expensive or impossible to repair. Consider asbestos, once a widely used material for insulation and fireproofing. It was later linked to life threatening adverse effects on human health. But for decades, lack of consensus among researchers delayed government action, and by the time bans on asbestos were enacted, millions had been exposed, leading to costly litigation, cleanup and preventable deaths.

records.transcript: If you've ever looked at a Picasso painting and thought, wait, is that a face or a guitar? You've already encountered the magic of cubism. This revolutionary movement shook up the art scene in the early 20th century. It wasn't just a new style. It was a complete reimagining of how we see and represent reality. Artists like Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque broke away from the traditional rules of perspective and instead chose to depict objects from multiple angles at once. Imagine seeing every side of a coffee cup, top, bottom and side, all in a single image. How is this coffee cup depicted? That's the kind of visual remix cubism brought to the canvas. At first, people didn't know what to make of it. Critics called it chaotic, even nonsensical. But over time, cubism proved to be a game changer, influencing not just painting and sculpture, but also music, literature and architecture. It encouraged creators to rethink structure, narrative and form, and to reconsider how we think about representation and abstraction. And it paved the way for other art movements, like modernism. Modernism also embraced abstraction and conceptual depth, though in somewhat different ways.

records.transcript: I once saw a video of a lionfish with its intimidating long spikes. Then it suddenly turned into a snake. Well, it turns out I was actually watching a mimic octopus. The mimic octopus lives in relatively shallow ocean water, and it's the first animal known to show dynamic mimicry, which means it can shift quickly between multiple imitations. Now, other creatures use mimicry. The owl butterfly's wings have markings resembling an owl's eye, which may keep the butterfly's predators away. But that's how the owl butterfly always looks. With dynamic mimicry, by contrast, an animal can shift its shape in real time. It contorts its body into different formations, often to confuse predators. A mimic octopus can imitate a lionfish or a snake. And it can quickly extend its arms and glide across the seafloor like a flatfish. But what use is changing shape if you can't also change color to look like a flatfish? Well, this octopus has cells called chromatophores just under its skin. Each chromatophore has a pigment inside it that could be red, yellow, etc. Uh, picture thousands of tiny balloons of different colors. If you stretch a balloon, it gets bigger, right? Well, the mimic octopus has muscles surrounding these chromatophores. They tighten to pull the necessary colors bigger and relax to make other colors smaller, making each color more or less visible. While this helps it hide from predators, it also aids in hunting, as unsuspecting prey often perceives the octopus as a non threatening species.

Well, this octopus has cells called chromatophores just under its skin.
Each chromatophore has a pigment inside it that could be red, yellow, etc.
Uh, picture thousands of tiny balloons of different colors.
If you stretch a balloon, it gets bigger, right?
Well, the mimic octopus has muscles surrounding these chromatophores.
They tighten to pull the necessary colors bigger and relax to make other colors smaller, making each color more or less visible.
While this helps it hide from predators, it also aids in hunting, as unsuspecting prey often perceives the octopus as a non threatening species.

records.transcript: Humans have been expressing themselves through art for thousands of years. Consider ancient cave paintings that have been discovered throughout the world, some of them more than 40,000 years old. Caves in Sulawesi, Indonesia, that include figurative art are an example of this. Some forms of art, though, have much more recent origins. Take, for example, decalcomania, a really cool art technique that originated in the 18th century. So what is decalcomania? At its core, it's a simple process. You begin by spreading paint onto a surface, like a sheet of paper. Then you press another surface, let's say canvas, onto the paper. So you press the two surfaces together. At this point you pull them apart while the paint is still wet. The resulting image is often rich with organic abstract patterns. Decalcomania was first used to decorate pottery in the 18th century, but it really took off in the 20th century, especially with the surrealist movement. Artists like Max Ernst loved this technique because it helped them tap into the subconscious and explore the unexpected. Ernst was enchanted by the process that allowed him to create shapes that the artist could not fully control. What's especially intriguing about decalcomania is the balance it strikes between control and chaos. Sure, the artist chooses the colours and the materials, but once the process is complete, the final result is mostly up to chance.

records.transcript: Have you ever been so engrossed in a task that you completely missed something obvious? This is called inattentional blindness, a phenomenon where concentrating on one thing can make us overlook something happening right in front of us. A classic study illustrates this perfectly. Participants watched a video of people passing a basketball and were asked to count passes made by players in white shirts. Midway through the video, a person in a gorilla suit walked into the scene, thumped its chest and left. Astonishingly, about half the viewers never saw the gorilla. Their attention was locked on counting passes. In real world situations, inattentional blindness can have serious consequences. For example, while driving, focusing on finding a street sign might make you miss a pedestrian stepping into the road. Recognizing this tendency can help us stay safer and more aware. Interestingly, psychologists trace this phenomenon to a useful ability, selective attention. This is the brain's way of filtering sensory input to avoid overload, allowing us to concentrate on important tasks. Think about sitting in a noisy open plan office writing a report. Phones are ringing, people are talking, but you managed to tune it all out and focus on your work. That's selective attention at its best.
records.translation:
你有没有过因为全神贯注于某项任务，而完全错过了显而易见的事情？
这被称为非注意性盲视，这是一种现象，即当我们专注于一件事时，可能会忽略眼前发生的事情。
一项经典研究完美地说明了这一点。
参与者观看了一段人们传篮球的视频，并被要求计算穿白衬衫的球员传球的次数。
视频进行到一半时，一个穿着大猩猩服装的人走入画面，捶打胸部后离开。
令人惊讶的是，大约一半的观众从未看到那只大猩猩。
他们的注意力完全集中在数传球次数上。
在现实世界中，非注意性盲视可能会带来严重的后果。
例如，开车时，专注于寻找路标可能会让你错过一个正在过马路的行人。
认识到这种倾向可以帮助我们保持更安全、更警觉。
有趣的是，心理学家将这种现象追溯到一种有用的能力——选择性注意力。
这是大脑过滤感官输入以避免超负荷，使我们能够专注于重要任务的方式。
想象一下，你坐在一个嘈杂的开放式办公室里写报告。
电话响个不停，人们在交谈，但你却设法屏蔽了所有这些，专注于自己的工作。
这就是选择性注意力的最佳体现。

records.transcript: Trilobites were a group of ancient sea creatures. They're classified as arthropods. They're extinct now. This is helpful for detecting motion, like noticing other creatures swimming around. Other types of compound eyes provided, say, sharper images. But having thousands of lenses was most common for trilobites. But in a recent study, researchers examined a trilobite fossil that was damaged. Part of its head was missing. This allowed them to notice, in the middle of the trilobite's forehead, 3 tiny dark spots, they said. These don't seem random. In fact, the tiny spots are evidence of a median eye, that is, a third eye. Most arthropods have median eyes, which aren't really like compound eyes. They're simpler. But a median eye had never been found in trilobites before. Why? Well, researchers had believed it was only there during the larval stage, early in the development of a young trilobite. So researchers thought adult fossils wouldn't have it. But it would have been hidden underneath a thin, dark layer of shell, which was missing in this fossil. So you wouldn't see it in a fossil whose entire head was intact.

records.transcript: The study of bioacoustics is a fascinating field that explores how living organisms produce and perceive sound. Bioacoustics encompasses a wide range of topics, from the songs of whales and birds to the communication methods of insects. Understanding these sounds can provide insights into animal behaviour and even aid in conservation efforts. For example, researchers have utilized bioacoustics to monitor whale populations. By recording and analyzing whale songs, scientists can track their movements and estimate population sizes. This information is vital for creating effective conservation strategies. Similarly, studying bird songs helps ornithologists understand mating rituals in territory establishment. These acoustic signals are often complex and specific to each species, providing a wealth of information about their social structures. Insects 2 use sounds for communication, particularly during mating. The chirping of crickets and buzzing of bees are examples of how bioacoustics plays a role in their life cycles. Despite its benefits, bioacoustics research faces challenges. The equipment needed for recording and analyzing sounds can be expensive and requires specialized knowledge to operate. Additionally, environmental noise such as traffic, machinery or even wind can interfere with the clarity of recordings, making it difficult to study certain species. Nonetheless, advancements in technology continue to improve the capabilities of bioacoustics, making it an invaluable tool for studying and protecting wildlife.

生物声学研究是一个引人入胜的领域，它探索生物体如何产生和感知声音。
生物声学涵盖了广泛的主题，从鲸鱼和鸟类的歌声到昆虫的交流方式。
了解这些声音可以帮助我们深入了解动物行为，甚至有助于保护工作。
例如，研究人员利用生物声学监测鲸鱼种群。
通过记录和分析鲸鱼的歌声，科学家可以追踪它们的活动并估计种群规模。
这些信息对于制定有效的保护策略至关重要。
同样，研究鸟类的歌声有助于鸟类学家了解它们的求偶仪式和领地建立。
这些声学信号通常复杂且因物种而异，为我们提供了关于它们社会结构的丰富信息。
昆虫也利用声音进行交流，尤其是在交配期间。
蟋蟀的鸣叫和蜜蜂的嗡嗡声是生物声学在其生命周期中发挥作用的例子。

录音和分析声音所需的设备可能昂贵，并且需要专业知识才能操作。
此外，交通、机械甚至风等环境噪声会干扰录音的清晰度，使得研究某些物种变得困难。
尽管如此，技术的进步不断提高了生物声学的能力，使其成为研究和保护野生动物的宝贵工具。

records.transcript: Today we're going to talk about the importance of sleep for cognitive function. Sleep is crucial for maintaining various aspects of brain health. One of the key benefits of sleep is the consolidation of memory. During sleep, particularly during the deep sleep stages, the brain processes and stores information acquired during the day, making it easier to recall later. During deep sleep, the brain also undergoes a process that flushes out neurotoxins like beta amyloid, which are linked to Alzheimer's disease. Sleep helps in learning new skills and knowledge by strengthening neural connections, and it allows the brain to enhance problem solving abilities by reorganizing information. Studies have shown that sleep deprivation affects cognitive functions like attention and decision making. Another crucial aspect of sleep is its role in emotional regulation. During sleep, the brain can process emotional experiences, which helps maintain emotional stability. REM sleep in particular plays a key role in recalibrating the brain's emotional circuits, helping people better manage fear and anxiety responses. People who do not get enough sleep are more likely to experience mood swings, anxiety, and depression. Despite the clear benefits of sleep, many people still struggle with getting enough rest. It's essential to prioritize sleep and adopt good sleep hygiene practices such as maintaining a regular sleep schedule, avoiding caffeine and electronic screens before bedtime, and creating a comfortable sleep environment. By doing so, individuals can improve their cognitive function and overall well being.

研究表明，睡眠不足会影响注意力和决策等认知功能。
睡眠的另一个关键方面是它在情绪调节中的作用。

优先考虑睡眠并采取良好的睡眠卫生习惯至关重要，例如保持规律的睡眠时间表，睡前避免咖啡因和电子屏幕，以及创造一个舒适的睡眠环境。

records.transcript: Positive reinforcement is a powerful concept in psychology and behavior training. It means giving a reward after someone performs an action you want them to do again. The basic idea is that when a behavior leads to a positive outcome, it's more likely to be repeated. In other words, we tend to repeat actions that bring us something positive. This principle applies to both humans and animals, but the way it works can differ. Animals need to receive rewards immediately after the desired behavior. For example, if a dog sits and gets a treat right away, it learns that sitting leads to something good. If the reward comes too late, the connection is lost. Humans, however, can understand delayed rewards. They might work hard today because they're aiming for a future goal, like earning a degree. Or they might feel motivated by praise even if the reward isn't tangible or instant. But rewards must be used carefully. If a parent gives a child candy to stop whining, the child may learn that whining gets rewarded. It's like watering weeds instead of flowers. You're encouraging the wrong behavior. And if rewards are given too frequently, they can reduce a person's internal motivation, making them rely more on external incentives to take action. So while positive reinforcement is effective, it works best when applied thoughtfully and with clear intent.

records.transcript: The Renaissance was a pivotal period in European history. Spanning roughly the 14th to the 17th centuries, the Renaissance is characterized by a renewed interest in art, science and literature. It marked a significant departure from the Middle Ages and laid the groundwork for the modern era. One of the defining features of the Renaissance was the revival of classical learning. Scholars and artists looked back to the texts and artistic achievements of ancient Greece and Rome for inspiration. This led to a flourishing of ideas and creativity evident in the works of figures like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo and Galileo Galilei. The invention of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440 was a crucial development during this time. It allowed for the mass production of books, making literature and scholarly works more accessible to a broader audience. This contributed to increased literacy and the spread of Renaissance ideas. The Renaissance also saw major advancements in science, particularly in astronomy. Nicolaus Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model of the solar system, placing the sun, not the Earth, as the center. Galileo Galilei later used a telescope to observe celestial bodies, providing evidence that supported Copernicus' theory. These discoveries challenged long held beliefs and laid the foundation for modern astronomy. Despite political instability in some regions, the Renaissance left a lasting legacy on European society. Its influence can still be seen today in art, science and education.
records.translation:

文艺复兴大致横跨14世纪到17世纪，其特点是对艺术、科学和文学重新产生了兴趣。
它标志着与中世纪的显著脱离，并为现代奠定了基础。
文艺复兴的决定性特征之一是古典学问的复兴。
学者和艺术家回溯古希腊和罗马的文本和艺术成就以获取灵感。
这导致了思想和创造力的繁荣，这在达芬奇、米开朗基罗和伽利略等人物的作品中显而易见。
约翰内斯·古腾堡在1440年左右发明的印刷术是这一时期的关键发展。
它使得书籍可以大规模生产，让文学和学术作品更广泛地传播给大众。
这促进了识字率的提高和文艺复兴思想的传播。
文艺复兴时期在科学领域也取得了重大进展，特别是在天文学方面。
尼古拉·哥白尼提出了太阳系的日心说模型，将太阳而非地球置于中心。
伽利略·伽利雷后来使用望远镜观察天体，为哥白尼的理论提供了证据。
这些发现挑战了长期以来的信念，并为现代天文学奠定了基础。
尽管一些地区存在政治不稳定，文艺复兴仍然对欧洲社会留下了持久的影响。
它的影响至今仍可在艺术、科学和教育领域看到。

records.transcript: Urbanization is frequently associated with negative outcomes: pollution, overcrowding and especially traffic congestion. In many cities, poor planning has led to increased noise and emissions as well as reduced quality of life. However, urbanization doesn't have to be this way. If approached thoughtfully, an alternative to traffic jams and congested city streets is to foster sustainable transportation. Copenhagen in Denmark, for instance, has made bicycles a central part of its urban design. The city's extensive network of protected bike lanes and pro cycling policies have encouraged residents to choose bicycles over cars. In addition to lowering automobile emissions, this shift has also improved public health and reduced traffic related stress. Also, when kept in control and planned properly, urbanization, in this case compact urban living, minimizes land use and energy consumption. Compared to sprawling suburban development, suburban neighborhoods require large plots of land for individual homes, roads and parking. When housing, services and infrastructure are concentrated, this can actually preserve surrounding natural areas and agricultural lands. So, even though this may seem strange, urban growth is actually more compatible with environmental conservation. Urbanization also, by necessity, has led to some innovative thinking, especially concerning the efficient use of land and space. Many cities are incorporating such innovation in food production by creating rooftop farms and using vertical agriculture, which grows crops in stacked vertical layers. In particular, Singapore has invested in high tech urban farming systems that grow vegetables in controlled environments, helping increase local food supply and reduce dependence on imports.
records.translation:
城市化经常与负面结果联系在一起：污染、过度拥挤，尤其是交通堵塞。
在许多城市，糟糕的规划导致噪音和排放增加，生活质量下降。
然而，城市化不一定非得如此。
如果深思熟虑，替代交通堵塞和拥挤城市街道的方法是促进可持续交通。
例如，丹麦的哥本哈根已将自行车作为其城市设计的核心部分。
该市广泛的受保护自行车道网络和支持骑自行车的政策鼓励居民选择自行车而不是汽车。
除了降低汽车排放外，这一转变还改善了公共健康，并减少了与交通相关的压力。
此外，如果控制得当并规划合理，城市化，在这种情况下是紧凑的城市生活，可以最大限度地减少土地使用和能源消耗。
与郊区无序扩张相比，郊区社区需要大块土地用于独立住宅、道路和停车场。
当住房、服务和基础设施集中时，这实际上可以保护周围的自然区域和农业用地。
所以，即使这看起来很奇怪，城市发展实际上与环境保护更兼容。
城市化也必然导致了一些创新思维，尤其是在土地和空间的有效利用方面。
许多城市正在通过建造屋顶农场和使用垂直农业（将作物种植在堆叠的垂直层中）将这种创新融入食品生产。
特别是，新加坡投资了高科技城市农业系统，在受控环境中种植蔬菜，帮助增加当地粮食供应并减少对进口的依赖。

Copenhagen in Denmark, for instance, has made bicycles a central part of its urban design.
The city's extensive network of protected bike lanes and pro cycling policies have encouraged residents to choose bicycles over cars.
In addition to lowering automobile emissions, this shift has also improved public health and reduced traffic related stress.
Also, when kept in control and planned properly, urbanization, in this case compact urban living, minimizes land use and energy consumption.
Compared to sprawling suburban development, suburban neighborhoods require large plots of land for individual homes, roads and parking.
When housing, services and infrastructure are concentrated, this can actually preserve surrounding natural areas and agricultural lands.
So, even though this may seem strange, urban growth is actually more compatible with environmental conservation.
Urbanization also, by necessity, has led to some innovative thinking, especially concerning the efficient use of land and space.
Many cities are incorporating such innovation in food production by creating rooftop farms and using vertical agriculture, which grows crops in stacked vertical layers.
In particular, Singapore has invested in high tech urban farming systems that grow vegetables in controlled environments, helping increase local food supply and reduce dependence on imports.

records.transcript: Throughout the years, archaeologists have discovered many fascinating artifacts on the Greek island of Crete. One example is the Phaistos disk, an ancient clay artifact that was found in the ruins of the Minoan palace at Phaistos. The Minoan civilization lasted from about 3100 BCE to 1100 BCE, and we think this artifact was made in the second millennium BCE. It was discovered in 1908, and it features many stamped symbols, 241 to be exact, in the shape of a spiral. The symbols include images of things like anemones, animals, tools, and so on. These animals, tools, and other images form a pattern in the shape of a spiral. What's so interesting is that these symbols are unlike anything else from the Minoan civilization or any other known writing system. Many experts have tried to decipher these enigmatic symbols. Some suggest they could represent an unknown language. Others think they might represent a calendar, or even a relic. Some believe they could represent a religious hymn. Yet, no consensus has been reached. Another intriguing thing about the Phaistos disk is the method used to imprint symbols. This involved pressing prefabricated stamps into wet clay. This process is really remarkable. It suggests a level of sophistication similar to early printing. Some scholars hypothesize that the disk might be an import, a loan artifact brought to Crete by traders or travelers. But this is another point of contention surrounding this fascinating artifact.

records.transcript: Today, we delve into the enigmatic world of outsider art, which refers to pieces created outside the boundaries of the traditional art world, by self taught artists. These artists typically work outside the mainstream, producing pieces that are raw, authentic, and deeply personal. Many creators of outsider art have faced personal challenges, which, in turn, have influenced their work. This gives their art a profound depth, often resonating deeply with audiences. An intriguing case is the work of James Castle, an artist who was born deaf and never learned to read, write, or speak. In his drawings, James Castle used soot from his wood stove and spit, saliva, as his primary materials, creating works that now hang in renowned galleries worldwide. What makes outsider art so compelling is its raw authenticity. But that same authenticity can be a barrier. Without formal training or gallery representation, outsider artists often struggle to gain visibility. Their work doesn't always fit into the neat categories curators and collectors expect, which means fewer exhibitions, less funding, and limited access to networks that could elevate their careers. The art world can be insular, favoring artists with art degrees, connections, or institutional backing. For outsiders, even getting a foot in the door can feel impossible. But here's the twist. Outsider art is often the most innovative and most emotionally resonant. It's art that doesn't ask for a price. It doesn't ask for permission. It just is. And that's exactly why it deserves more space, more support, and more recognition.

records.transcript: Desertification is the process by which fertile land transforms into desert, typically as a result of drought, deforestation or unsustainable agricultural practices. One significant driver of desertification is the over exploitation of land for intensive agriculture. This can exhaust soil nutrients, diminish vegetation cover and accelerate erosion. Without root systems to anchor the soil, wind and water strip away topsoil, leaving behind barren land. In some cases, monoculture farming and excessive irrigation also contribute by disrupting natural soil chemistry. Deforestation further intensifies desertification. When forests are cleared for timber or agricultural expansion, the absence of trees reduces the land's capacity to retain moisture. This loss of canopy cover not only dries out the soil, but also disrupts local rainfall patterns, compounding the desert spread. Climate change is another accelerating force. Rising global temperatures and shifting precipitation cycles lead to prolonged droughts and extreme weather events, placing additional stress on soil and vegetation. records.transcript: Today we're discussing the concept of dark stores. That is, retail centers that resemble warehouses and are usually located near city centers. Unlike traditional storefronts, they are not designed for walk in customers, but function as fulfillment hubs optimized for rapid online delivery. The rise of dark stores has been fueled by the growing demand for online shopping, especially in urban areas where space is limited and rent is high. The main appeal of dark stores lies in their efficiency. By eliminating the traditional storefront, businesses can reduce overhead costs and pass savings on to consumers through lower prices. Their proximity to dense urban areas also allows for faster delivery times, meeting the expectations of customers who value speed and convenience. For instance, a company might deliver groceries in under an hour, giving it a major competitive advantage over traditional supermarkets. However, dark stores are not without drawbacks. Their expansion can contribute to the decline of traditional retail spaces, creating economic challenges for local businesses. Employment is another concern. While these centers generate jobs in logistics and delivery, they may reduce the number of customer facing roles available in physical stores. Looking ahead, many experts predict that dark stores will continue to reshape the retail landscape. Some may adopt advanced automation, further reducing the need for human labor and potentially redefining the shopping experience itself. As with other technological shifts, the key challenge will be balancing efficiency with the broader social and economic implications of these changes.

今天我们讨论一下“暗店”的概念。

有些可能会采用先进的自动化技术，进一步减少对人力的需求，并可能重新定义购物体验本身。
正如其他技术变革一样，主要挑战将是平衡效率与这些变革更广泛的社会和经济影响。

records.transcript: We've been talking about the law of inertia. An object moving in a straight line will continue to move in a straight line unless it is acted upon by another force. So what does this mean in the real world? Let's look at something many people do all the time: riding a bicycle. Think about riding along in a straight line. Once the bike is moving, inertia will keep it going in a straight line. But we don't just ride in straight lines, do we? We turn at corners and steer around things that are in our way. So how do you get the bicycle not to go straight? Easy, right? Don't you just need to turn the front wheel in the direction you want to turn? In fact, if you only turn the front wheel, you're likely to end up on the pavement. The wheel will turn, but because of inertia, your body and the rest of the bike will want to keep moving straight ahead. So how does a cyclist avoid this? The key is to lean in. Weight needs to shift in the direction of the turn so that the force of gravity can work against the force of inertia. Professional cyclists who move at high speeds need to hit a sweet spot. They must lean more to keep their bicycles from sliding out of turns, but not too much. At a certain point, gravity will bring both rider and bicycle down to the ground.
records.translation:
我们一直在讨论惯性定律。
一个物体沿直线运动，除非受到其他力的作用，否则它将继续沿直线运动。
那么这在现实世界中意味着什么呢？
让我们来看看很多人一直在做的事情：骑自行车。
想象一下沿着直线骑行。
一旦自行车启动，惯性就会使其沿直线行驶。
但我们不只是沿着直线骑行，对吗？
我们在拐角处转弯，并绕开路上的障碍物。
那么你如何让自行车不走直线呢？
很简单，对吧？
难道你不需要把前轮转向你想要转弯的方向吗？
事实上，如果你只转动前轮，你很可能会摔倒在人行道上。
车轮会转动，但由于惯性，你的身体和自行车的其余部分会想要继续向前直行。
那么骑自行车的人如何避免这种情况呢？
关键在于倾斜身体。
需要将重心向转弯方向转移，这样重力才能对抗惯性力。
高速骑行的专业自行车手需要找到一个最佳平衡点。
他们必须倾斜更多以防止自行车在转弯时滑出，但又不能倾斜过多。
在某个点上，重力会将骑手和自行车都带到地面。

records.transcript: For most of its history, the scientific field of anthropology, the study of culture, put humans at the center, often in ways that now seem narrow and limiting. Animals were treated as resources, symbols, or mere background, important only for what they meant to us. Classic anthropology focused on how people hunted, herded, or mythologized animals, reinforcing a sharp divide. Humans belonged to culture, animals to nature. For example, early studies of Arctic hunting rituals examined how seals symbolized spiritual beliefs and social bonds without asking about the seals' own behaviors or ecological roles. This approach gave us insight into human meaning making, but it overlooked the complexity of interspecies relationships. Multispecies anthropology flips that perspective. It sees humans and other species, animals, plants, even fungi, as co participants in shared worlds. Instead of reducing nonhumans to cultural symbols, it highlights their agency, their ability to act, adapt, and influence human lives. Take the studies of mushroom foraging in Siberia. Here fungi, trees, and humans form interdependent networks. The growth of matsutake mushrooms depends on and reflects forest health and human harvesting practices, even as harvesting practices and forest health are influenced by the mushrooms themselves. The point is, life isn't a human story with animals or plants in the background. It's a web of relationships among many kinds of beings. Next, I'll explore how this multispecies perspective reshapes research methods, what it means to study not just human cultures, but the entangled lives of humans and other beings.
records.translation:
在其历史的大部分时间里，人类学这一文化研究的科学领域都以人类为中心，其方式现在看来往往是狭隘和局限的。
动物被视为资源、符号或仅仅是背景，只有当它们对我们有意义时才显得重要。
经典人类学关注人们如何狩猎、放牧或神化动物，从而强化了一种鲜明的划分。
人类属于文化，动物属于自然。
例如，早期对北极狩猎仪式的研究考察了海豹如何象征精神信仰和社会联系，但并未探究海豹自身的行为或生态作用。
这种方法让我们洞察了人类的意义建构，但它忽视了物种间关系的复杂性。
多物种人类学颠覆了这种视角。
它将人类和其他物种，包括动物、植物乃至真菌，视为共享世界中的共同参与者。
它不再将非人类简化为文化符号，而是强调它们的能动性，即它们行动、适应和影响人类生活的能力。
以西伯利亚采蘑菇的研究为例。
在这里，真菌、树木和人类形成了相互依存的网络。
松茸的生长依赖并反映了森林健康和人类采摘习惯，反之，采摘习惯和森林健康也受到蘑菇本身的影响。
重点是，生命不是一个以动物或植物为背景的人类故事。
它是一个由多种生命形式组成的关系网。
接下来，我将探讨这种多物种视角如何重塑研究方法，以及研究的意义不再仅仅是人类文化，而是人类与其他生命形式纠缠不清的生活。

records.transcript: The Eastgate Centre in Harare, Zimbabwe, is a mixed complex combining retail spaces and offices. When the architect Mick Pearce was asked to design the building in the early 1990s, he faced a big challenge: how to keep all its shops and offices cool without traditional air conditioning and do it during an economic crisis. Energy costs were high and importing advanced air conditioners was impossible. To solve this dilemma, Pearce looked to termite mounds. Termites are insects that live in large colonies. They build big mounds on the ground throughout the African savanna. The mounds are amazing structures. Some rise 3 meters above ground and extend another one to three meters below the ground. The underground chambers connect to the above ground chimneys through a maze of tunnels, and this entire system works like natural climate control. Warm air rises and escapes through the top, while cooler air flows in from below. The thick walls of soil and clay absorb heat during the day and release it at night. Termites fine tune airflow by opening and closing vents, adding or removing soil to enlarge or seal passages. On hot days, they open more vents for cooling. At night, they close them to keep warm. Then, Pearce borrowed these ideas. The Eastgate Centre's walls are made from thick materials like concrete and brick, and there's a system of ducts and adjustable louvers throughout the building to mimic those vents. The result? A building that uses far less energy than its conventional counterparts.

能源成本高昂，进口先进空调又是不可能的。

晚上，它们会关闭通风口以保持温暖。

东门中心的墙壁由混凝土和砖块等厚重材料制成，整个建筑内部有一个管道和可调节百叶窗系统，以模仿那些通风口。

这座建筑比传统同类建筑节省了大量能源。

records.transcript: We've been talking about the law of inertia. An object moving in a straight line will continue to move in a straight line unless it is acted upon by another force. So what does this mean in the real world? Let's look at something many people do all the riding a bicycle. Think about riding along in a straight line. Once the bike is moving, inertia will keep it going in a straight line. But we don't just ride in straight lines, do we? We turn at corners and steer around things that are in our way. So how do you get the bicycle not to go straight? Easy, right? Don't you just need to turn the front wheel in the direction you want to turn? In fact, if you only turn the front wheel, you're likely to end up on the pavement. The wheel will turn, but because of inertia, your body and the rest of the bike will want to keep moving straight ahead. So how does a cyclist avoid this? The key is to lean in. Weight needs to shift in the direction of the turn so that the force of gravity can work against the force of inertia. Professional cyclists who move at high speeds need to hit a sweet spot. They must lean more to keep their bicycles from sliding out of turns, but not too much. At a certain point, gravity will bring both rider and bicycle down to the ground.

records.transcript: If you've ever looked at a Picasso painting and thought, wait, is that a face or a guitar, you've already encountered the magic of cubism. This revolutionary movement shook up the art scene in the early 20th century. It wasn't just a new style. It was a complete reimagining of how we see and represent reality. Artists like Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque broke away from the traditional rules of perspective and instead chose to depict objects from multiple angles at once. Imagine seeing every side of a coffee cup, top, bottom and side, all in a single image. How is this coffee cup depicted? That's the kind of visual remix cubism brought to the canvas. At first, people didn't know what to make of it. Critics called it chaotic, even nonsensical. But over time, cubism proved to be a game changer, influencing not just painting and sculpture, but also music, literature and architecture. It encouraged creators to rethink structure, narrative and form, and to reconsider how we think about representation and abstraction. And it paved the way for other art movements, like modernism. Modernism also embraced abstraction and conceptual depth, though in somewhat different ways.

它不仅仅是一种新风格。
它彻底重塑了我们看待和表现现实的方式。
像巴勃罗·毕加索和乔治·布拉克这样的艺术家打破了传统的透视规则，转而选择一次性从多个角度描绘物体。
想象一下，在一个图像中看到咖啡杯的每一面，顶部、底部和侧面，都在一张图片中。
这个咖啡杯是如何被描绘的？
这就是立体主义带给画布的视觉混搭。
起初，人们不知所措。
评论家称其混乱，甚至荒谬。
但随着时间的推移，立体主义被证明是一个颠覆者，不仅影响了绘画和雕塑，还影响了音乐、文学和建筑。
它鼓励创作者重新思考结构、叙事和形式，并重新审视我们对再现和抽象的看法。
它也为其他艺术运动铺平了道路，比如现代主义。
现代主义也接受了抽象和概念深度，尽管方式有所不同。

transcriptSentences.text: If you've ever looked at a Picasso painting and thought, wait, is that a face or a guitar, you've already encountered the magic of cubism.
This revolutionary movement shook up the art scene in the early 20th century.
It wasn't just a new style.
It was a complete reimagining of how we see and represent reality.
Artists like Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque broke away from the traditional rules of perspective and instead chose to depict objects from multiple angles at once.
Imagine seeing every side of a coffee cup, top, bottom and side, all in a single image.
How is this coffee cup depicted?
That's the kind of visual remix cubism brought to the canvas.
At first, people didn't know what to make of it.
Critics called it chaotic, even nonsensical.
But over time, cubism proved to be a game changer, influencing not just painting and sculpture, but also music, literature and architecture.
It encouraged creators to rethink structure, narrative and form, and to reconsider how we think about representation and abstraction.
And it paved the way for other art movements, like modernism.
Modernism also embraced abstraction and conceptual depth, though in somewhat different ways.

records.transcript: Let's talk a little about sea otters and their importance to their own and indeed other ecosystems. We'll start with a few basic facts. The sea otter is a marine mammal often found along the coastal waters of the northern Pacific. It lacks the blubber of other marine mammals like whales, say, or seals. But it stays warm in icy waters thanks to its fur, which is the densest of any animals. It also has unusually large lungs, two and a half times larger than those of similarly sized land mammals. And this helps it stay buoyant and dive efficiently. Sea otters have a loose flap of skin under each forearm that functions like a pocket, which they use for storing food and tools. That's right. Tools. Sea otters are one of the few animals that use tools, using clamshells for digging and rocks to open clamshells. Now, wonderful as they may be, why care about sea otters? Because sea otters eat sea urchins and sea urchins eat kelp. Kelp is a large seaweed that can grow up to 30 meters tall, providing food and shelter for a range of marine life. Kelp forests support a greater variety of marine life than almost any other ocean habitat. Kelp also grows very densely and acts as a natural buffer, protecting shorelines from storm damage. Finally, kelp forests are like rainforests in that they absorb and store carbon dioxide through photosynthesis, mitigating climate change and reducing ocean acidification.

我们来谈谈海獭以及它们对自己和其他生态系统的重要性。
我们先从一些基本事实说起。
海獭是一种海洋哺乳动物，通常生活在北太平洋的沿海水域。
它不像其他海洋哺乳动物，比如鲸鱼或海豹，那样有鲸脂。
但它能在冰冷的海水中保持温暖，多亏了它的皮毛，这是所有动物中最浓密的。
它还有异常大的肺，比同等大小的陆地哺乳动物的肺大两倍半。
这有助于它保持浮力并有效地潜水。
海獭每只前臂下方都有一块松散的皮肤，像一个口袋，它们用它来储存食物和工具。
没错。
工具。
海獭是少数使用工具的动物之一，它们用蛤蜊壳挖洞，用石头撬开蛤蜊壳。
那么，海獭虽然很可爱，但为什么要关心它们呢？
因为海獭吃海胆，海胆吃海带。
海带是一种大型海藻，可以长到30米高，为各种海洋生物提供食物和住所。
海带森林支持的海洋生物种类比几乎任何其他海洋栖息地都多。
海带也生长得非常茂密，并作为天然屏障，保护海岸线免受风暴损害。
最后，海带森林就像雨林一样，通过光合作用吸收和储存二氧化碳，从而减缓气候变化并减少海洋酸化。

transcriptSentences.text: Let's talk a little about sea otters and their importance to their own and indeed other ecosystems.
We'll start with a few basic facts.
The sea otter is a marine mammal often found along the coastal waters of the northern Pacific.
It lacks the blubber of other marine mammals like whales, say, or seals.
But it stays warm in icy waters thanks to its fur, which is the densest of any animals.
It also has unusually large lungs, two and a half times larger than those of similarly sized land mammals.
And this helps it stay buoyant and dive efficiently.
Sea otters have a loose flap of skin under each forearm that functions like a pocket, which they use for storing food and tools.
That's right.
Tools.
Sea otters are one of the few animals that use tools, using clamshells for digging and rocks to open clamshells.
Now, wonderful as they may be, why care about sea otters?
Because sea otters eat sea urchins and sea urchins eat kelp.
Kelp is a large seaweed that can grow up to 30 meters tall, providing food and shelter for a range of marine life.
Kelp forests support a greater variety of marine life than almost any other ocean habitat.
Kelp also grows very densely and acts as a natural buffer, protecting shorelines from storm damage.
Finally, kelp forests are like rainforests in that they absorb and store carbon dioxide through photosynthesis, mitigating climate change and reducing ocean acidification.

records.transcript: In recent years, more people have started growing plants in urban spaces, a practice known as urban gardening. This includes cultivating plants on rooftops, balconies and in community gardens. Urban gardening can help reduce some negative effects of urbanisation such as pollution. One benefit is improved air quality. Plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which helps clean the air and make cities more liveable. Another advantage is enhanced food security. By growing their own produce, city residents can access fresh, healthy food and rely less on commercial agriculture. This is especially helpful in food deserts, areas where access to fruits and vegetables is limited. Imagine an abandoned plot in a city, maybe a piece of land where an old factory used to be. Now imagine clearing the land and building a small community centre surrounded by garden plots. People from the neighbourhood come to workshops to learn how to plant and cultivate spinach, strawberries, tomatoes, whatever produce they want. These neighbourhood volunteers then cultivate the garden plots and harvest their produce. As you can imagine, this would bring people together and encourage cooperation and shared responsibility. However, there are challenges to urban gardening, such as soil contamination. In some instances, the soil may contain harmful substances like heavy metals or industrial chemicals. Gardeners often need to test and treat the soil or use raised beds with clean soil to ensure safe growing conditions. Despite these obstacles, cities are adopting policies to support urban gardening and improve residents' quality of life.
records.translation:
近年来，越来越多的人开始在城市空间种植植物，这种做法被称为城市园艺。
这包括在屋顶、阳台和社区花园种植植物。
城市园艺有助于减少城市化的一些负面影响，例如污染。
一个好处是改善空气质量。
植物吸收二氧化碳并释放氧气，这有助于净化空气，使城市更宜居。
另一个优势是增强食品安全。
通过种植自己的农产品，城市居民可以获得新鲜、健康的食物，并减少对商业农业的依赖。
这在“食物荒漠”中特别有用，即水果和蔬菜供应有限的地区。
想象一下城市中一块废弃的土地，也许是一块旧工厂曾经所在地。
现在想象一下清理这块土地，建造一个小社区中心，周围环绕着花园地块。
附近的居民会来参加讲习班，学习如何种植和栽培菠菜、草莓、西红柿，或者任何他们想要的农产品。
这些社区志愿者随后耕种花园地块并收获他们的农产品。
正如你可以想象的，这将把人们聚集在一起，鼓励合作和共同责任。
然而，城市园艺也面临挑战，例如土壤污染。
在某些情况下，土壤可能含有有害物质，如重金属或工业化学品。
园艺师通常需要检测和处理土壤，或者使用带有清洁土壤的抬高花坛，以确保安全的种植条件。
尽管存在这些障碍，城市仍在采纳政策来支持城市园艺，改善居民的生活质量。

transcriptSentences.text: In recent years, more people have started growing plants in urban spaces, a practice known as urban gardening.
This includes cultivating plants on rooftops, balconies and in community gardens.
Urban gardening can help reduce some negative effects of urbanisation such as pollution.
One benefit is improved air quality.
Plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which helps clean the air and make cities more liveable.
Another advantage is enhanced food security.
By growing their own produce, city residents can access fresh, healthy food and rely less on commercial agriculture.
This is especially helpful in food deserts, areas where access to fruits and vegetables is limited.
Imagine an abandoned plot in a city, maybe a piece of land where an old factory used to be.
Now imagine clearing the land and building a small community centre surrounded by garden plots.
People from the neighbourhood come to workshops to learn how to plant and cultivate spinach, strawberries, tomatoes, whatever produce they want.
These neighbourhood volunteers then cultivate the garden plots and harvest their produce.
As you can imagine, this would bring people together and encourage cooperation and shared responsibility.
However, there are challenges to urban gardening, such as soil contamination.
In some instances, the soil may contain harmful substances like heavy metals or industrial chemicals.
Gardeners often need to test and treat the soil or use raised beds with clean soil to ensure safe growing conditions.
Despite these obstacles, cities are adopting policies to support urban gardening and improve residents' quality of life.

records.transcript: So today we're looking at the hero's journey, a storytelling pattern that shows up in myths, literature, and narratives from all over the world. This structure was brought into the spotlight by Joseph Campbell, an American mythologist. In his book, The Hero with a Thousand Faces, Campbell studied myths across cultures and noticed they shared a common structure. Campbell called it the monomyth, and he believed it reflected something universal about the human experience. The journey usually kicks off with a call to adventure, some kind of invitation or challenge that pulls the hero out of their everyday life. They might resist at first, but eventually they accept, often with a mentor's help. Then come the trials, tests that push the hero to grow. At the center of it all is the abyss, the toughest part, where the hero faces their greatest fear or enemy. If they make it through, they're transformed. And here's the key part. They return with a gift, some kind of insight, wisdom, or ability that can help others. That gift is what makes the journey meaningful, not just for the hero, but for their community. Some critics argue this model oversimplifies storytelling. It can flatten out cultural differences and force diverse stories into a single mold. Still, I'd argue it's influential because it taps into something deeply human. The idea that struggle leads to growth and that we come back changed.

今天我们要探讨的是英雄之旅，这是一种在世界各地的神话、文学和叙事中都出现的讲故事模式。
这种结构是由美国神话学家约瑟夫·坎贝尔提出的。
在他的著作《千面英雄》中，坎贝尔研究了不同文化的神话，并注意到它们共享一个共同的结构。
坎贝尔称之为“一元神话”，他认为这反映了人类经验的一些普遍性。
这段旅程通常以“冒险的召唤”开始，这是一种将英雄从日常生活中拉出来的邀请或挑战。
他们可能一开始会抵制，但最终会接受，通常是在导师的帮助下。
然后是考验，这些考验促使英雄成长。
一切的核心是深渊，最艰难的部分，英雄在此面对他们最大的恐惧或敌人。
如果他们成功度过，他们就会得到蜕变。
这就是关键部分。
他们带着一份礼物归来，某种可以帮助他人的洞察力、智慧或能力。
这份礼物让这段旅程变得有意义，不仅对英雄本人，也对他们的社区。
一些评论家认为这种模式过分简化了讲故事的方式。
它可能会抹平文化差异，将多样化的故事强行纳入一个单一的模式中。
不过，我认为它之所以有影响力，是因为它触及了人类内心深处的一些东西。
即斗争带来成长，我们因此而改变的想法。

records.transcript: Let's talk about lean manufacturing and its impact on efficiency in production processes. Lean manufacturing is a systematic approach to minimizing waste within a manufacturing system while maximizing productivity. While the methodology has been adopted by many companies worldwide, it was developed by a Japanese carmaker in the mid 20th century. But its roots can actually be traced to the supermarket. In the 1950s, Japanese engineers observed that supermarkets in the United States only restocked items as customers purchased them, maintaining just enough inventory to meet demand. This idea of just in time inventory management became a core principle of lean manufacturing. By identifying and removing excess inventory and eliminating other inefficiencies, companies could reduce costs and increase their overall productivity. Another important aspect of lean manufacturing is continuous improvement, often referred to as kaizen. This involves constantly seeking ways to enhance processes, products and services. Companies at all levels are encouraged to contribute ideas for improvement, fostering a culture of innovation and teamwork. Lean manufacturing also emphasizes the importance of value from the customer's perspective. Companies focus on producing goods that meet customer needs and expectations, ensuring that each step in the production process adds value rather than unnecessary complexity. As you might imagine, implementing lean manufacturing requires a shift in organizational culture. Resistance to change and difficulty in sustaining improvements can get in the way. That said, companies that successfully adopt lean practices experience increased efficiency, reduced costs and higher customer satisfaction.
records.translation:
我们来谈谈精益制造及其对生产过程效率的影响。
精益制造是一种系统性的方法，旨在最大限度地减少制造系统中的浪费，同时最大限度地提高生产力。
虽然这种方法已被全球许多公司采用，但它是由一家日本汽车制造商在20世纪中期开发的。
但它的根源实际上可以追溯到超市。
在20世纪50年代，日本工程师观察到美国超市只在顾客购买商品时才补货，只维持足够的库存以满足需求。
这种即时库存管理理念成为精益制造的核心原则。
通过识别和消除过剩库存并消除其他低效率，公司可以降低成本并提高整体生产力。
精益制造的另一个重要方面是持续改进，通常被称为“改善”（kaizen）。
这包括不断寻找方法来改进流程、产品和服务。
鼓励各级公司贡献改进的想法，培养创新和团队合作的文化。
精益制造还强调从客户角度看价值的重要性。
公司专注于生产满足客户需求和期望的产品，确保生产过程中的每一步都增加价值，而不是不必要的复杂性。
正如你可能想象的，实施精益制造需要组织文化的转变。

transcriptSentences.text: Let's talk about lean manufacturing and its impact on efficiency in production processes.
Lean manufacturing is a systematic approach to minimizing waste within a manufacturing system while maximizing productivity.
While the methodology has been adopted by many companies worldwide, it was developed by a Japanese carmaker in the mid 20th century.
But its roots can actually be traced to the supermarket.
In the 1950s, Japanese engineers observed that supermarkets in the United States only restocked items as customers purchased them, maintaining just enough inventory to meet demand.
This idea of just in time inventory management became a core principle of lean manufacturing.
By identifying and removing excess inventory and eliminating other inefficiencies, companies could reduce costs and increase their overall productivity.
Another important aspect of lean manufacturing is continuous improvement, often referred to as kaizen.
This involves constantly seeking ways to enhance processes, products and services.
Companies at all levels are encouraged to contribute ideas for improvement, fostering a culture of innovation and teamwork.
Lean manufacturing also emphasizes the importance of value from the customer's perspective.
Companies focus on producing goods that meet customer needs and expectations, ensuring that each step in the production process adds value rather than unnecessary complexity.
As you might imagine, implementing lean manufacturing requires a shift in organizational culture.
Resistance to change and difficulty in sustaining improvements can get in the way.
That said, companies that successfully adopt lean practices experience increased efficiency, reduced costs and higher customer satisfaction.

records.transcript: Most wind instruments, which are played by blowing into them, went through lots of modifications before becoming the standardized instruments we see and hear today. Now, most brass instruments, like the trumpet and trombone, underwent many centuries of refinement before being standardized. But the tuba only took about 180 years to reach its current form. That's because, through centuries, composers and inventors wanted an ideal bass instrument to play those really low notes. Rather than tinker with an instrument they didn't love, they'd discard it and start again. So the tuba doesn't really have a clear ancestor, more a series of prototypes. An early example was the serpent. The serpent was made of a wooden tube, bent into the shape of, well, a serpent. The letter S. Problem was, it didn't sound great. The wooden tube was too wide, which caused problems with intonation, meaning it was hard to hit the right notes. Imagine a choir of voices accompanied by a serpent, booming along out of tune. Ouch. Well, so long, serpent. And hello, ophicleide. The ophicleide's main advantage was that it was made of brass. The brass construction made its intonation much better. The ophicleide became much more popular than the serpent. The composer Berlioz used it in some famous pieces. But still, the ophicleide wasn't the answer. Its pitch range was pretty narrow, and composers wanted something that could play lower notes.

records.transcript: Imagine that you have a full time job, but you want to take a year off to go back to school. What is it going to cost you? Of course, there's the cost of tuition for your classes, plus living expenses. But what about the money you're no longer earning at your job because you're now a student? We call that the opportunity cost. Opportunity cost refers to the value of the next best alternative that must be given up when making a choice. It's a fundamental principle in economics that helps individuals and businesses understand the true cost of their decisions. My exercise in imagination illustrates a personal decision, but businesses also face opportunity costs in their operations. For instance, a company may choose to invest in new equipment rather than spend money to expand its product line. The opportunity cost of this decision is the potential revenue that could have been generated from the new products. Understanding opportunity cost helps individuals, as well as businesses, make informed decisions that maximize their benefits and minimize their losses. It's important to note that opportunity cost is not always measured in financial terms. It can also be related to factors like time, convenience, or personal satisfaction. For that reason, opportunity cost can be difficult to quantify, especially when dealing with non monetary factors. Have you ever had to make a decision that included an opportunity cost? Take a few minutes now to think, and then I'll ask for volunteers to share.

records.transcript: Today I want to tell you about an unusual phenomenon that scientists noticed in the Pacific Ocean in the early 1990s. The scientists were recording sounds using hydrophones positioned on the ocean floor in the North Pacific. Hydrophones are specially designed microphones that allow scientists to collect acoustic data underwater. While most of the undersea noise picked up by the hydrophones emanated from whales, ships' engines, or earthquakes, the scientists monitoring the hydrophones detected a number of sounds that they could not identify. One was a regular series of rising infrasonic tones, that is, of very short wavelengths, below those humans can hear. The scientists labeled these very low frequency noises upsweep. At first, these sounds were thought to be the songs of whales migrating in the Pacific. However, scientists who study whale acoustics eventually ruled out this possibility, and the origin of the upsweep sounds remained unknown. So, what is this, the source of the rising tones detected by the hydrophones? The sounds were ultimately tracked to an area of inferred volcanic seismic activity, a chain of undersea mountains in the South Pacific. Some scientists believe that, if these mountains contain an active volcano, the source for the mysterious upsweep sounds may be hot volcanic lava coming in contact with cold seawater.

records.transcript: In the early 1900s, sea otters, marine mammals that feed on invertebrates including sea urchins, were nearly wiped out along the United States Pacific coast by fur hunters. With otters gone, urchin numbers exploded, destroying kelp forests. Kelp is a type of seaweed, and it's sea urchins' favorite food. This left countless marine species without the protective habitat that kelp forests provided to them. In 1972, hunting sea otters was banned. As otters made a comeback, urchin numbers dropped, kelp forests grew back, and biodiversity flourished. Scientists realized otters were a keystone species, organisms whose impact on ecosystems is far greater than their numbers suggest. A similar case occurred in Yellowstone National Park. Wolves, the park's top predator, had been eradicated. Populations of elk, a deer like animal and a favorite prey for wolves, soared. And their huge populations damaged local vegetation, including the willow and aspen trees for which the park had been famous. In the 1990s, wolves were reintroduced to the park to get the elk population under control. But the wolves didn't just cut elk numbers. They changed elk behavior. Afraid of being eaten by wolves, the elk avoided streamside areas where they're especially vulnerable. This helped willow and aspen trees reestablish themselves there. And the trees brought back beavers, animals that live in streams and build dams to create ponds for themselves. The beaver dams created habitats for fish, birds, and amphibians, a huge cascading effect because of this other keystone species.
